sections.h2: Tax offices at 223 North Spalding Avenue
sections.html:
Lebanon's county government offices for taxes sit under one address, 223 North Spalding Avenue, so a Marion County owner can finish most paperwork in a single trip. Suite numbers tell you where to go.

  • Sheriff's Office, Suite 101 (270-692-3051): bills and payments, weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, Suite 202 (270-692-3401): value, name and address changes, and exemption filings, on those same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk, Suite 102 (270-692-2651): deed recording and delinquent bills. The clerk's own site lists 8:20 to 4:20 on weekdays and a Saturday morning session.

Questions about value or how a bill was figured get routed to the PVA. Anyone asking about delinquent bills, or about buying a lien, is sent to the clerk.

Marion County is thinly settled, with roughly 57 people per square mile on 343 square miles of land. Lebanon, the seat, is the largest of three cities, followed by Loretto and Bradfordsville. One school district, Marion County Schools, serves every address.

A century of slow growth left the population at 19,820 in 2010 and 19,581 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate of 20,115 is 2.8 percent above the 2020 base. The county has 8,652 housing units and 7,724 households. Owners occupy 77.7 percent of homes, and over nine in ten people lived at the same address a year earlier. The median home value is $168,100, median gross rent is $726, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $1,243 a month. Only 56 building permits were issued in 2025, which leaves resale listings with little new competition.

Selling a farm adds a twist. Section 172A of the state constitution values crop and pasture land by its yield. Outbuildings and fencing are priced at replacement cost less wear. Before you set an asking price on a farm, have the PVA tell you how each acre is classed.

The sheriff mails statements ahead of October 1. If nothing has arrived by October 10, call the office and ask for a duplicate.

Marion County sheriff collection calendar
Payment windowWhat you pay
Oct. 1 through Nov. 1Face amount minus two percent
Nov. 2 through Dec. 31Face amount
All of JanuaryFive percent added
Feb. 1 through Apr. 15Twenty-one percent added
After Apr. 15Balance goes to the clerk

Anything unpaid on April 16 moves to the County Clerk. The twenty-one percent combines the ten percent penalty of KRS 134.015 to the sheriff's collection add-on.

Write the bill number on a mailed check, and enclose a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt. Card payments are taken only at the counter, with the card company's fee charged to you. Partial payments are not tracked by the sheriff's system, so pay the full amount in one go.

sections.h2: Who pays when the house sells
sections.html:
That year's bill carries the name of the January 1 owner. Once the house sells, the sheriff expects the seller to forward the bill to the buyer, and a buyer who never got one can request a copy from the office. The office carries no responsibility when a bill is missed during a closing.

No copy goes to the mortgage servicer. The homeowner gets each bill and has to pass it to the lender in time.

For earlier years, call the clerk at 270-692-2651. Overdue bills are transferred there, and the clerk's site advertises a free Online Deed Room. KRS 134.420 lets a tax lien stay on the land for eleven years, so a title company will insist that it be paid from the seller's proceeds.

Call 270-692-3401 and ask for a conference. The meeting is the required first step of any appeal under state law, and KRS 133.120 then sends an unresolved case to the clerk as a written petition and on to a hearing. KRS 133.030 opens that hearing between 25 and 35 days after inspection wraps up.

PVA staff are expected to inspect every Marion County parcel in person within four years, so ask when yours was last visited. Appraisals and nearby sales carry weight. Payment stays due on the amount you claim.

Before the meeting, gather what a stranger would need to agree with you: photos of the house, an appraisal if you have one, repair estimates, and the prices of nearby homes that sold. Write down the value you think is fair and be ready to explain how you reached it. If the sit-down does not change the number, the petition to the clerk is your next step, and the clerk will tell you when the hearing is set.

For 2025 and 2026 the exemption takes $49,100 off assessed value. The PVA takes applications from owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who live in the house. About 19.5 percent of Marion County residents are 65 or older, so the exemption reaches a sizable share of owners. It stays with the owner, so a buyer applies separately. Take proof of age or a disability classification with you, and ask what else the office needs so one visit is enough. After a mid-year sale, let the PVA know so the exemption comes off the house you no longer own.

sections.h2: Recording a deed at the clerk's counter
sections.html: The clerk first collects the grantor's transfer tax, which KRS 142.050 sets at fifty cents for every $500 of value or part of $500. Taxes paid at the clerk's counter can use cash, check, debit or credit card, and the clerk's site warns that cards carry extra fees. No tax is due on foreclosure sales, on transfers between spouses in a divorce, or on a parent's deed to a child for token payment.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller with a tax question
sections.html:
Begin at the sheriff's counter in Suite 101 and ask if this year's bill is paid. Then walk down the hall to the clerk in Suite 102 and ask whether any earlier year was transferred there. Finish at the PVA in Suite 202, where you can check the owner name, mailing address and any exemption on the roll.

Request each balance in writing along with the date it is good through, because interest and penalties shift the figure as weeks pass. The title agent takes those letters and pays every amount from your proceeds at closing. Cash deals can move fast, so get the payoff papers ready before you accept an offer.

If you inherited the property, check whose name the roll shows, and bring proof of your authority to act for the estate. The office will not guess who should receive a bill, so a name change on the roll keeps statements from going astray before the sale.

faqs.q: Where is the Marion County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: Go to 223 North Spalding Avenue, Suite 101, in Lebanon, or phone 270-692-3051. Put the bill number on any payment you mail.

faqs.q: How much extra does a Marion County bill cost in February?
faqs.a: Twenty-one percent is added between February 1 and April 15, following 5 percent in January. A bill still open on April 16 moves to the clerk.

faqs.q: Does the Marion County sheriff accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's system does not track partial payments, so send the full bill in one payment.

faqs.q: Which office handles Marion County exemptions?
faqs.a: The PVA, reachable at 270-692-3401. Homestead and disability questions get sent there by the sheriff.

faqs.q: Where do I look up a Marion County delinquent bill?
faqs.a: Phone the County Clerk, 270-692-2651, since overdue bills are transferred to that office. Its website also offers a free Online Deed Room.
